subject.title: [Bug]: Cron isolated agentTurn skips delivery before dispatch when a recovered early tool error is classified as fatal

question: For an isolated cron session that ends successfully after a child process actually ran and exited nonzero, should OpenClaw use a persisted degraded/warning run outcome that may still dispatch final output, rather than infer success from final text or report a terminal error?
rationale: The maintainer has rejected text-based recovery as unsafe, while the remaining proposal changes durable cron status, delivery-state semantics, alerting, and retry/backoff behavior; source-level implementation cannot safely choose that product contract unilaterally.

options.title: Approve typed degraded delivery
options.body: Add typed process-start/failure-phase evidence and a degraded cron outcome that preserves warnings but can attempt delivery when the approved final-deliverable criteria hold.

options.title: Keep terminal-error semantics
options.body: Continue treating process-ran nonzero exits as terminal for cron delivery, while improving records to distinguish not-attempted delivery from provider send failure.

options.title: Narrow the eligible recovery class
options.body: Define a smaller typed subset of failures that may degrade and deliver, leaving all other process-exit failures terminal.

recommendation.title: Approve typed degraded delivery
recommendation.body: Add typed process-start/failure-phase evidence and a degraded cron outcome that preserves warnings but can attempt delivery when the approved final-deliverable criteria hold.

likelyOwner.reason: The assigned member has already articulated the safety boundary and required design direction in the issue discussion.
